gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-noto-san: Noto Sans Mono gives sturdy, large-looking words generous spacing, so every curve stays open and no two letters ever bump together. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its keep big and short.
Love Ya Like A Sister draws round letters like bent wire. Noto Sans Mro sets dense, tall-looking words with wide entrances, and that wiry-versus-sturdy gap is the pair's best trait.
Spaghetti strokes, all one width, give Love Ya Like A Sister its loud, expressive look. Noto Sans Nushu stands beneath it with terminals held far from the stroke and a towering x-height.
Neon-glass tubing becomes lettering in Love Ya Like A Sister. Noto Sans Old Italic does the quieter work, keeping lowercase close to capital height and curve endings well apart.
Loud, steady lines: Love Ya Like A Sister never changes stroke weight. Noto Sans Old Permic backs it with rounded forms open to the side, and lowercase nearly as tall as capitals.
A level, quiet beat runs through Love Ya Like A Sister, bold yet without any accents of weight. Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau reads smoothly, its open curves never crowding.
Noto Sans Tai Viet keeps ascenders short and the x-height tall, with terminals pulled back from each curve's closing point. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its place big and brief.

Expressive thread-work: Love Ya Like A Sister stitches its strokes along a path. Big, short lines suit Love Ya Like A Sister, while Noto Sans Tamil, terminals stopping far from the stem, carries the rest.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-stack-sans-text: Stack Sans Text draws a marker-like constant line. Gugi is the showoff, cutting terminals open so counters flow outward, while that body keeps its big-bodied lowercase tidy, curve endings well apart.
gen-gf-metamorphous-gf-comme: Commanding in tone, Metamorphous has large sidebearings and a high-set midline. Comme, with lowercase filling most of the letter height, can be sized down a notch without losing its smooth read.
